rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite subject with an affirmative predicate can restrict the predicate; here, after Solomon rejects the offer, بل means that they alone rejoice in their gift, denying that he rejoices in it.
rows.anchor: فإن المقصود نفي فرحه هو بالهدية لا إثبات الفرح لهم بهديتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The named subject can make the affirmative predicate exclusive: the phrase means that only God knows them.
rows.anchor: أي لا نعلمهم إلا نحن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fronted subject with a negative predicate makes the negation stronger than predicate-only negation and can also convey restriction.
rows.anchor: فإنه أبلغ في نفي الكذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite subject with an affirmative predicate restricts by kind (a man, not a woman) or number (one man, not two).
rows.anchor: نحو ( رجل جاءني ) فيفيد التخصيص إما بالجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting negation immediately before the subject restricts the negation: Moses is not dear to them, although his clan is; he asks whether they value his clan over God.
rows.anchor: أي العزيز علينا رهطك لا أنت ولذا قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti presents the preceding constructions as the substance of ʿAbd al-Qahir's view, followed by al-Sakkaki with added conditions and detail.
rows.anchor: هذا حاصل رأي الشيخ عبد القاهر ووافقه السكاكي وزاد شروطا وتفاصيل

rows.speaker: الشيخ بهاء الدين
rows.claim: Emphasis without restriction is distinguished from restrictive emphasis only by the demands of context and discourse.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ بهاء الدين ولا يتميز ذلك إلا بما يقتضيه الحال وسياق الكلام

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير وابن النفيس
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir, Ibn al-Nafis, and others say that placing the predicate before the subject conveys exclusivity.
rows.anchor: ذكر ابن الأثير وابن النفيس وغيرهما أن تقديم الخبر على المبتدأ يفيد الاختصاص

rows.speaker: صاحب الفلك الدائر
rows.claim: The author reports that the author of al-Falak al-Daʾir rejects this rule, claiming no one held it.
rows.anchor: ورده صاحب الفلك الدائر بأنه لم يقل به أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti rejects that objection: al-Sakkaki and others explicitly say fronting an element normally delayed gives restriction, as in “Tamimi am I.”
rows.anchor: وهو ممنوع فقد صرح السكاكي وغيره بأن تقديم ما رتبته التأخير يفيده

rows.speaker: السكاكي
rows.claim: Al-Sakkaki says that explicitly mentioning the subject can convey restriction.
rows.anchor: ذكر السكاكي أنه قد ذكر ليفيد التخصيص

rows.speaker: صاحب الإيضاح
rows.claim: The author of al-Idah objects to al-Sakkaki's claim that mentioning the subject conveys restriction.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه صاحب الإيضاح

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explicitly treats the named subject as restrictive in examples from al-Raʿd, al-Zumar, and al-Ahzab.
rows.anchor: وصرح الزمخشري بأنه أفاد الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When reports say a verse was revealed about different matters, the wording may mean interpretation rather than occasion of revelation; there is no conflict if the verse includes both.
rows.anchor: فإن عبر أحدهم بقوله نزلت في كذا والآخر نزلت في كذا وذكر أمرا آخر فقد تقدم أن هذا يراد به التفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If one report explicitly identifies a cause and another merely says the verse concerns a matter, the explicit cause is authoritative and the latter is inference; Ibn Umar's claim about anal intercourse is treated this way, with Jabir's report preferred and Ibn Abbas also correcting him.
rows.anchor: فالمعتمد حديث جابر لأنه نقل وقول ابن عمر استنباط منه وقد وهمه فيه ابن عباس

rows.speaker: جندب
rows.claim: The Two Sahihs and others transmit from Jundub that after the Prophet was ill and missed prayer for a night or two, a woman said his devil had abandoned him, and the Duha verses were revealed.
rows.anchor: مثاله ما أخرجه الشيخان وغيرهما عن جندب اشتكى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلم يقم ليلة أو ليلتين

rows.speaker: خولة
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet's former household servant says a dead puppy beneath a bed kept Gabriel away for four days; after Khawla cleaned it out, the Prophet received revelation from Duha through “until you are pleased.”
rows.anchor: وكانت خادم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن جروا دخل بيت النبي

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar calls the puppy story famous but its status as the cause of Duha strange, since its chain includes an unknown narrator; he prefers the report in the Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن حجر في شرح البخاري قصة إبطاء جبريل بسبب الجرو مشهورة لكن كونها سبب نزول الآية غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tafwit is presenting varied meanings, such as praise and description, in separate sentences of equal measure; it may use long, medium, or short sentences.
rows.anchor: هو إتيان المتكلم بمعان شتى من المدح والوصف وغير ذلك من الفنون كل فن في جملة منفصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's successive statements about God's guidance, provision, healing, death, and revival exemplify al-tafwit in long sentences.
rows.anchor: فمن الطويلة ﴿ الذي خلقني فهو يهدين والذي هو يطعمني ويسقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence about night and day and the living and dead is the medium-length example of al-tafwit.
rows.anchor: ومن المتوسطة ﴿ تولج الليل في النهار وتولج النهار في الليل

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
rows.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isbaʿ says the Qur'an has no al-tafwit example composed of short sentences.
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي الاصبع ولم يأت المركب من القصيرة في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first group of prohibitions ends with “so that you may reason”: shirk, disobedience to parents, infanticide despite God's provision, indecency, and killing from rage all oppose sound judgment and reason's recognition of God's oneness.
rows.anchor: لأن الوصايا التي في الآية الأولى إنما يحمل على تركها عدم العقل الغالب على الهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The financial and verbal duties end with “so that you may remember”: people know how they want others to treat their own orphans and dealings, while neglect comes from failing to reflect on this reciprocity.
rows.anchor: فلذلك ناسب الختم بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to follow God's religious law ends with “so that you may guard yourselves,” meaning guard against God's punishment for abandoning it.
rows.anchor: وأما الثالثة فلأن ترك اتباع شرائع الله الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement about stars ends with “for people who know” because calculating by and navigating with the stars is the work of those skilled in that knowledge.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن حساب النجوم والاهتداء بها يختص بالعلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of human creation and movement from loins to womb, worldly life, life, and death ends “for people who understand,” since reflection on these subtle stages requires deeper comprehension.
rows.anchor: والنظر في ذلك والفكر فيه أدق فناسب ختمه

words: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of abundant provision, crops, and fruits ends “for people who believe,” since recognizing these blessings should lead to faith and gratitude.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر ما أنعم به على عباده من سعة الأرزاق والأقوات والثمار وأنواع ذلك ناسب ختمه بالإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two orphan boys are identified as Asram and Sarim.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لغلامين يتيمين ﴾ هما أصرم وصريم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The one who called to Mary from beneath her is identified as Jesus.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فناداها من تحتها ﴾ قيل عيسى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification of the one who called to Mary from beneath her is Gabriel.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فناداها من تحتها ﴾ قيل عيسى وقيل جبريل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The human who says this is identified as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ويقول الإنسان ﴾ هو أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification is Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: هو أبي بن خلف وقيل أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further alternative identification is al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
rows.anchor: وقيل أمية بن خلف وقيل الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who disbelieved is al-As ibn Wa'il.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أفرأيت الذي كفر ﴾ هو العاصي بن وائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person Moses killed was a Copt named Faq'un.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وقتلت نفسا ﴾ هو القبطي وإسمه فاقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan is named Musa ibn Zafar.
rows.anchor: ﴿ السامري ﴾ إسمه موسى بن ظفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger whose trace was taken is Gabriel.
rows.anchor: ﴿ من أثر الرسول ﴾ هو جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who disputes about God is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ومن الناس من يجادل ﴾ هو النضر بن الحارث

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: A report in both Sahih collections from Abu Dharr identifies the two parties as Hamza, Ubayda ibn al-Harith, and Ali against ʿUtba, Shayba, and al-Walid ibn ʿUtba.
rows.anchor: أخرج الشيخان عن أبي ذر قال نزلت هذه الآية في حمزة وعبيدة بن الحارث وعلي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person who intends wrongdoing in the sanctuary is ʿAbd Allah ibn Unays.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت في عبد الله بن أنيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who brought the slander are Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthatha, Hamna bint Jahsh, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, who bore its chief burden.
rows.anchor: هم حسان بن ثابت ومسطح بن أثاثة وحمنة بنت جحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer who bites his hands on that day is ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt.
rows.anchor: هو عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person called “so-and-so” is identified as Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: ﴿ لم أتخذ فلانا ﴾ هو أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification of “so-and-so” is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: هو أمية بن خلف وقيل أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi identifies the unbeliever as Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وكان الكافر ﴾ قال الشعبي هو أبو جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The woman who rules them is Bilqis, daughter of Sharahil.
rows.anchor: ﴿ امرأة تملكهم ﴾ هي بلقيس بنت شراحيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who came to Solomon was named Mundhir.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فلما جاء سليمان ﴾ إسم الجائي منذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ifrit from among the jinn was named Kawzan.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال عفريت من الجن ﴾ إسمه كوزن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one possessing knowledge is Asif ibn Barkhiya, Solomon's scribe.
rows.anchor: هو آصف بن برخيا كاتبه وقيل رجل يقال له ذو النور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identity for the one possessing knowledge is a man called Dhu al-Nur.
rows.anchor: وقيل رجل يقال له ذو النور

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identity is Ustum.
rows.anchor: وقيل أسطوم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identity is Malikha.
rows.anchor: وقيل مليخا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identity is Balkh.
rows.anchor: وقيل بلخ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identity is Dabba, ancestor of the tribe.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو ضبة أبو القبيلة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identity is Gabriel.
rows.anchor: وقيل جبريل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identity is a different angel.
rows.anchor: وقيل ملك آخر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identity is al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine men are Rami, Raʿim, Harmi, Harim, Daʾb, Sawab, Raʾb, Mistah, and Qudar ibn Salif, killer of the she-camel.
rows.anchor: هم رعمى ورعيم وهرمى وهريم ودأب وصواب ورأب ومسطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who picked Moses up was named Tabuth.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فالتقطه آل فرعون ﴾ إسم الملتقط طابوث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's wife was Asia bint Muzahim.
rows.anchor: ﴿ امرأة فرعون ﴾ آسية بنت مزاحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' mother was Yahandh, daughter of Yashhar ibn Lawi.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أم موسى ﴾ يحانذ بنت يصهر بن لاوى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reported name for Moses' mother is Yaʾ wa Kha.
rows.anchor: وقيل ياء وخا وقيل أباذخت

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative reported name for Moses' mother is Abadhkht.
rows.anchor: وقيل ياء وخا وقيل أباذخت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' sister was named Maryam.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وقالت لأخته ﴾ إسمها مريم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reported name for Moses' sister is Kulthum.
rows.anchor: إسمها مريم وقيل كلثوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Makkan reading recommends takbir from al-Duha through the end of the Qur'an; a report traces the instruction through Ibn Abi Bazzah, Ikrima, Ismaʿil al-Makki, Ibn Kathir, Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
rows.anchor: يستحب التكبير من الضحى إلى آخر القرآن وهي قراءة المكيين

rows.speaker: الحاكم
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi first transmits the practice as stopped at a Companion, then gives a raised report; al-Hakim also authenticates the raised route, and al-Bazzi has many routes for it.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه من هذا الوجه أعني المرفوع الحاكم في مستدركه وصححه وله طرق كثيرة عن البزي

rows.speaker: محمد بن إدريس الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Bazzi reports al-Shafiʿi saying that abandoning takbir would mean losing one of the Prophet's sunnas; Ibn Kathir takes this as implying al-Shafiʿi authenticated the report.
rows.anchor: قال لي محمد بن إدريس الشافعي إن تركت التكبير فقدت سنة من سنن نبيك

rows.speaker: أبو العلاء الهمداني
rows.claim: A report says revelation paused, the polytheists said God had abandoned Muhammad, then Duha was revealed and the Prophet made takbir; Ibn Kathir says its chain cannot be graded sound or weak.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم انقطع عنه الوحي فقال المشركون قلا محمدا ربه فنزلت سورة الضحى فكبر النبي

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Halimi explains takbir as analogous to the takbir after completing Ramadan's fast; one pauses after each surah and says “Allahu akbar.”
rows.anchor: نكتة التكبير التشبيه للقراءة بصوم رمضان إذا أكمل عدته يكبر

rows.speaker: سليم الرازي
rows.claim: Sulaym al-Razi says to say takbir between each pair of surahs, with a pause separating it from the preceding surah; non-takbir readers fear habituation may make people think it is Qur'an.
rows.anchor: يكبر بين كل سورتين تكبيرة ولا يصل آخر السورة بالتكبير بل يفصل بينهما بسكتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nashr records disagreements over whether takbir begins at the start or end of Duha, ends at the start or end of al-Nas, and joins or separates from either surah; these depend on whether takbir belongs to the surah's beginning or end.
rows.anchor: اختلف القراء في ابتدائه هل هو من أول الضحى أو من آخرها وفي انتهائه هل هو أول سورة الناس أو آخرها

rows.speaker: السخاوي وأبو شامة
rows.claim: The transmitted takbir wording is either “Allahu akbar” or “There is no god but God, and God is greatest”; al-Sakhawi and Abu Shama say the practice applies inside and outside prayer.
rows.anchor: وفي لفظه فقيل الله أكبر وقيل لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر وسواء في التكبير في الصلاة وخارجها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام
rows.claim: Abu Ubayd reconciles the disagreement: some Qur'anic words had foreign origins, but Arabs naturalized them into Arabic before revelation, so both the Arabic and foreign-origin claims are true.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام بعد أن حكى القول بالوقوع عن الفقهاء والمنع عن العربية

rows.speaker: الجواليقي وابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Al-Jawaliqi, Ibn al-Jawzi, and others favor Abu Ubayd's reconciliation of Arabic usage with foreign etymology.
rows.anchor: ومال إلى هذا القول الجواليقي وابن الجوزي وآخرون

rows.speaker: الثعالبي والجواليقي
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿalibi calls abariq Persian; al-Jawaliqi says the loan means a water channel or pouring water gently.
rows.anchor: أباريق حكى الثعالبي في فقه اللغة أنها فارسية وقال الجواليقي الإبريق فارسي معرب

rows.speaker: شيذلة
rows.claim: Shidhla reports that ab means grass in the language of people of the Maghrib.
rows.anchor: أب قال بعضهم هو الحشيش بلغة أهل الغرب حكاه شيذلة

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says iblaʿi means “swallow” in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن وهب بن منبه في قوله

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, transmitting from his father, gives an Indian gloss for iblaʿi: “drink.”
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ من طريق جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه قال اشربي بلغة الهند

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says akhlada ila al-ard means “inclined to the earth” in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي في الإرشاد أخلد إلى الأرض ركن بالعبرية

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi reports that ara'ik means couches in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: الأرائك حكى ابن الجوزي في فنون الأفنان أنها السرر بالحبشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azar is included among the alleged foreign-derived words by those who do not take it as the proper name of Abraham's father or the idol.
rows.anchor: آزر عد في المعرب على قول من قال إنه ليس بعلم لأبي إبراهيم ولا للصنم

rows.speaker: معتمر بن سليمان
rows.claim: Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman says he heard his father recite Azar in the accusative and report that it means “crooked”; some say it is their-language abuse meaning “you who err.”
rows.anchor: ذكر عن معتمر بن سليمان قال سمعت أبي يقرأ

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth says asbat means tribes in the language of the non-Arabs, corresponding to the Arabic word for tribes.
rows.anchor: أسباط حكى أبو الليث في تفسيره أنها بلغتهم كالقبائل بلغة العرب

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses istabraq as thick brocade in the Persian language.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك أنه الديباج الغليظ بلغة العجم

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says asfar means books in Syriac.
rows.anchor: أسفار قال الواسطي في الإرشاد هي الكتب بالسريانية

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak also glosses asfar as books, but identifies the language as Nabataean.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن الضحاك قال هي الكتب بالنبطية

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim says isr means “covenant” in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: إصري قال أبو القاسم في لغات القرآن معناه عهدي بالنبطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qasas opens with Moses' story, rescue, refusal to aid criminals, and flight from his homeland; it closes by telling the Prophet not to aid unbelievers, consoling him over expulsion from Mecca, and promising his return, recalling “We shall return him.”
rows.anchor: وانظر إلى سورة القصص كيف بدئت بأمر موسى ونصرته

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari notes the contrast between al-Mu'minun's opening, “The believers have succeeded,” and its close, “The disbelievers do not succeed”; al-Kirmani gives the same observation.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري وقد جعل الله فاتحة سورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat Sad begins with mention and ends by calling the Qur'an a reminder to all worlds.
rows.anchor: وقال في سورة ( ص ) بدأها بالذكر وختمها به في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat Nun begins by denying that the Prophet is mad by his Lord's grace and closes with the disbelievers' accusation that he is mad.
rows.anchor: وفي سورة ( ن ) بدأها بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A surah's opening may connect verbally with the preceding surah's close; the Elephant's “eaten straw” is followed by Quraysh's “for the security of Quraysh.”
rows.anchor: ومنه مناسبة فاتحة السورة لخاتمة ما قبلها حتى أن منها

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash describes the connection between the Elephant's ending and Quraysh's opening as a syntactic connection, like “so that they might be enemies and grief” in the Moses story.
rows.anchor: فقد قال الأخفش اتصالها بها من باب

rows.speaker: الكواشي
rows.claim: Al-Kawashi says al-Ma'ida's opening command to fulfill covenants reinforces al-Nisa's closing command to monotheism and justice among people.
rows.anchor: وقال الكواشي في تفسير المائدة لما ختم سورة النساء أمرا بالتوحيد والعدل بين العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Anʿam's opening praise suits the preceding al-Ma'ida's close on divine judgment, echoed by the praise after judgment in 39:75.
rows.anchor: مناسب لختام المائدة من فصل القضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatir's opening praise fits Saba's close describing separation from what people desired, and is illustrated by the praise after the destruction of wrongdoers in 6:45.
rows.anchor: وكافتتاح سورة فاطر بالحمد لله فإنه مناسب لختام ما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hadid opens with glorification, matching al-Waqiʿa's close with the command to glorify the Lord's name.
rows.anchor: وكافتتاح سورة الحديد بالتسبيح فإنه مناسب لختام سورة الواقعة بالأمر به

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha says the forms “in hadhani,” “al-muqimin,” and “al-sabi'un” are the work of scribes who erred in writing; Abu Ubayd's chain for her report is sound on the standards of the Two Sahihs.
rows.anchor: حدثنا أبو معاوية عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال سألت عائشة عن لحن القرآن

rows.speaker: عثمان
rows.claim: A report from ʿIkrima says Uthman found grammatical irregularities in the codices but ordered them left intact, saying Arabs would correct or Arabize them; related versions are transmitted by Ibn al-Anbari and Ibn Ashta.
rows.anchor: لما كتبت المصاحف عرضت على عثمان فوجد فيها حروفا من اللحن فقال لا تغيروها

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr read al-muqimin al-salata and called it a scribal grammatical error.
rows.anchor: من طريق أبي بشر عن سعيد بن جبير أنه كان يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti says the reports are deeply problematic: the Companions were eloquent, especially in speech, so attributing grammatical errors to them is implausible.
rows.anchor: وكيف يظن بالصحابة أولا أنهم يلحنون في الكلام فضلا عن القرآن وهم الفصحاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that the Companions received the Qur'an from the Prophet as revealed, memorized, mastered, and accurately preserved it, making scribal error in it implausible.
rows.anchor: الذي تلقوه من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كما أنزل وحفظوه وضبطوه وأتقوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is implausible that all the Companions jointly made and wrote the same error, then failed to notice or correct it.
rows.anchor: اجتماعهم كلهم على الخطأ وكتابته ثم كيف يظن بهم رابعا عدم تنبههم ورجوعهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti asks how Uthman could have ordered an error left unchanged and how a mistaken reading could then persist through continuous mass transmission.
rows.anchor: ثم كيف يظن بعثمان أنه ينهي عن تغييره ثم كيف يظن أن القراءة استمرت على مقتضي ذلك الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti deems this impossible rationally, legally, and customarily; the first scholarly answer is that the report from Uthman is unsound because its chain is weak, disrupted, and disconnected.
rows.anchor: وقد أجاب العلماء عن ذلك بثلاثة أجوبة أحدها أن ذلك لا يصح عن عثمان فإن إسناده ضعيف مضطرب منقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first answer also argues that Uthman established an authoritative codex to follow, so it is unlikely he would retain an obvious error for later Arabs to fix; multiple identical copies make a shared error unlikely, while no one reports differing codices except for valid reading variants.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان الذين تولوا جمعه وكتابته لم يقيموا ذلك وهم الخيار فكيف يقيمه غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the Qur'an's four central proofs of inimitability are predictions of unseen future events that later occurred as foretold.
rows.anchor: الثالث ما انطوى عليه من الإخبار بالمغيبات وما لم يكن فوجد كما ورد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further central proof is the accurate account of ancient peoples, scriptures, and laws unknown to an unlettered Prophet except to rare lifelong scholars of the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: الرابع ما أنبأ به من أخبار القرون السالفة والأمم البائدة والشرائع الداثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an challenged the Jews to wish for death if truthful, foretold they would never do so, and none accepted the challenge; the author treats this as part of the third proof.
rows.anchor: فما تمناه أحد منهم وهذا الوجه داخل في الوجه الثالث

words: أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِقُونَ
rows.speaker: جبير بن مطعم
rows.claim: Jubayr ibn Mutʿim says hearing the Prophet recite al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, especially its questions through “al-musaitirun,” made his heart nearly fly and first rooted Islam in it.
rows.anchor: كما وقع لجبير بن مطعم أنه سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقرأ في المغرب بالطور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people died upon hearing Qur'anic verses, and works have been devoted to documenting these cases.
rows.anchor: وقد مات جماعة عند سماع آيات منه أفردوا بالتصنيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is a lasting sign that will endure as long as the world, with God guaranteeing its preservation.
rows.anchor: ومن وجوه إعجازه كونه آية باقية لا يعدم ما بقيت الدنيا مع تكفل الله بحفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its recitation does not weary readers or repel listeners: repetition increases sweetness and affection, unlike ordinary speech; a report calls it something that does not wear out through repeated recitation.
rows.anchor: لا يمله وسامعه لا يمجه بل الإكباب على تلاوته يزيده حلاوة وترديده يوجب له محبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an gathers knowledge no book can contain in few words; this belongs under eloquence, while the preceding four forms are the actual grounds of inimitability and the other features are virtues and distinctive qualities.
rows.anchor: قال وهذا الوجه داخل في بلاغته فلا يجب أن يعد فنا مفردا في إعجازه

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi estimates Qur'anic sciences by multiplying its words by four—outer meaning, inner meaning, limit, and point of access—yielding vast totals, and says combinations and relations are beyond counting or human knowledge.
rows.anchor: علوم القرآن خمسون علما وأربعمائة علم وسبعة آلاف علم وسبعون ألف علم على عدد كلم القرآن مضروبة في أربعة

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi divides Qur'anic knowledge into monotheism (creatures and God's names, attributes, and acts), reminder (promise, threat, afterlife, and purification), and rulings (duties, benefits, harms, commands, prohibitions, and recommendations).
rows.anchor: وأما علوم القرآن فثلاثة توحيد وتذكير وأحكام

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: For Ibn al-Arabi, al-Fatiha is the Qur'an's mother because it contains all three domains, while al-Ikhlas is a third because it contains monotheism alone.
rows.anchor: ولذلك كانت الفاتحة أم القرآن لأن فيها الأقسام الثلاثة وسورة الإخلاص ثلثه

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir identifies three Qur'anic subjects—monotheism, reports, and religious law—and says al-Ikhlas is a third because it contains all of monotheism.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جرير القرآن يشتمل على ثلاثة أشياء التوحيد والإخبار والديانات

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa enumerates thirty Qur'anic subjects, including signs, analogy, commands and prohibitions, promise and threat, paradise and hell, divine names and acts, gratitude, argument, ethics, wisdom, praise, blame, and moral instruction.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى القرآن يشتمل على ثلاثين شيئا الإعلام والتشبيه والأمر والنهي والوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: شيذلة
rows.claim: Shidhla says Ibn Jarir's three categories encompass Ali ibn Isa's list and much more, because the Qur'an's wonders cannot be exhausted or counted.
rows.anchor: وقال شيذلة وعلى التحقيق إن تلك الثلاثة التي قالها ابن جرير تشمل هذه كلها بل أضعافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Suyuti says every foundational kind of knowledge and issue is indicated in God's Book, which also contains creation's wonders, the heavens and earth, the highest horizon and what is beneath the soil, origins, messengers, angels, and histories of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: قد اشتمل كتاب الله العزيز على كل شيء أما أنواع العلوم فليس منها باب ولا مسألة هي أصل إلا وفي القرآن ما يدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As evidence, al-Suyuti lists Qur'anic narratives including Adam and Iblis, Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, Jonah, Shuʿayb, Lot, Tubbaʿ, the people of the Trench, Abraham and Nimrod, and Ishmael's settlement and the building of the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: وعيون أخبار الأمم السالفة كقصة آدم مع إبليس في إخراجه من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His list also includes Moses' birth, casting into the river, killing the Copt, journey to Midian and marriage, revelation at the Mount, confrontation with Pharaoh, and the calf and other episodes.
rows.anchor: قصة موسى في ولادته وإلقائه في اليم وقتل القبطي ومسيره إلى مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man from Moses' faction is identified as the Samaritan.
rows.anchor: ﴿ هذا من شيعته ﴾ هو السامري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man from Moses' enemy is named Fatun.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وهذا من عدوه ﴾ إسمه فاتون

words: وَجَآءَ رَجُلٌۭ مِّنْ أَقْصَا ٱلْمَدِينَةِ يَسْعَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who came running from the far end of the city is the believer from Pharaoh's people, named Shamaʿan, Shamaʿun, Jabr, Habib, or Hizqil.
rows.anchor: هو مؤمن آل فرعون وإسمه شمعان وقيل شمعون وقيل جبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two women tending the flock are Liya and Safuriya; one is the woman Moses married.
rows.anchor: هما ليا وصفوريا وهي التي نكحها وأبوهما شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their father is identified as Shuʿayb.
rows.anchor: وأبوهما شعيب وقيل يثرون ابن أخي شعيب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says their father is Yathrun, Shuʿayb's nephew.
rows.anchor: وقيل يثرون ابن أخي شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman's son is called Baran, Daran, Anʿam, or Mashkam.
rows.anchor: إسمه باران بالموحدة وقيل داران وقيل أنعم وقيل مشكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Azra'il is widely used for the Angel of Death; Abu al-Shaykh ibn Hibban transmits it from Wahb.
rows.anchor: اشتهر على الألسنة أن اسمه عزرائيل ورواه أبو الشيخ بن حبان عن وهب

words: أَفَمَن كَانَ مُؤْمِنًۭا كَمَن كَانَ فَاسِقًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse distinguishing believer from transgressor was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Walid ibn ʿUqba.
rows.anchor: نزلت في علي بن أبي طالب والوليد بن عقبة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the two men from Banu Haritha seeking leave from the Prophet as Abu ʿAraba ibn Aws and Aws ibn Qayzi.
rows.anchor: قال السدي هما رجلان من بني حارثة أبو عرابة بن أوس وأوس بن قيظي

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the Prophet then had nine wives—Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habiba, Sawda, Umm Salama, Safiyya, Maymuna, Zaynab bint Jahsh, and Juwayriya—and four daughters: Fatima, Zaynab, Ruqayya, and Umm Kulthum.
rows.anchor: قال عكرمة كانت تحته يومئذ تسع نسوة عائشة وحفصة وأم حبيبة وسودة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies the people of the household as Ali, Fatima, Hasan, and Husayn.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم هم علي وفاطمة والحسن والحسين

words: لِلَّذِىٓ أَنْعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَأَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person God and the Prophet favored is Zayd ibn Haritha, and the wife he is told to retain is Zaynab bint Jahsh.
rows.anchor: هو زيد بن حارثة ﴿ أمسك عليك زوجك ﴾ هي زينب بنت جحش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the human who bore the trust as Adam.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وحملها الإنسان ﴾ قال ابن عباس هو آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two messengers sent to the people are identified as Simon and John, with Paul as the third.
rows.anchor: هما شمعون ويوحنا والثالث بولس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative names the messengers Sadiq, Saduq, and Shalum.
rows.anchor: وقيل هم صادق وصدوق وشلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who came from the far end of the city is Habib al-Najjar.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وجاء من أقصى المدينة رجل ﴾ هو حبيب النجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human mentioned is identified as al-As ibn Wa'il.
rows.anchor: هو العاص بن وائل وقيل أبي بن خلف وقيل أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative identification is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقيل أبي بن خلف وقيل أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative identification is Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: وقيل أبي بن خلف وقيل أمية بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boy announced as good news is identified either as Ishmael or Isaac, two famous views.
rows.anchor: هو إسماعيل أو إسحاق قولان شهيران

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The disputants are said to be two angels, Gabriel and Michael.
rows.anchor: هما ملكان قيل إنهما جبريل وميكائيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The body placed on Solomon's throne is identified as a devil called Usayd.
rows.anchor: هو شيطان يقال له أسيد وقيل صخر وقيل حبقيق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative name for the devil is Sakhr.
rows.anchor: هو شيطان يقال له أسيد وقيل صخر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative name for the devil is Huqayq.
rows.anchor: هو شيطان يقال له أسيد وقيل صخر وقيل حبقيق

rows.speaker: نوف
rows.claim: Nawf says the Satan who afflicted Job was called Musaʿat.
rows.anchor: قال نوف الشيطان الذي مسه يقال له مسعط
